content:
Leo (support): FYI — customer on Private/VPC deploy reporting failures during bootstrap: apt and pip fail, container pull errors, and model pulls time out. They see TLS/OCSP and 403s. Suspect egress block from their firewall. Can SRE/devops confirm a minimal allowlist?

Maria SRE: Got it. Do we have a repro snippet from their infra? If they can run a couple quick checks that helps: `curl -v https://files.pythonhosted.org/simple/` and `curl -v https://archive.ubuntu.com/ubuntu/` also `openssl s_client -connect files.pythonhosted.org:443 -status` to show OCSP stapling.

Leo (support): Paste from customer — short log excerpt:```
$ pip install -r requirements.txt
Collecting requests
  Could not fetch URL https://pypi.org/simple/requests/: 
  Unknown error: <urlopen error [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed: Hostname mismatch or OCSP response missing>

$ apt-get update
Err:1 http://archive.ubuntu.com/ubuntu focal InRelease
  TLS handshake failed: TLSv1.2 alert protocol version

$ docker pull ghcr.io/company/image:latest
Error response from daemon: received unexpected HTTP status: 403 Forbidden
```
They also ran `openssl s_client -connect files.pythonhosted.org:443 -status` and got:```
OCSP response: no response sent
verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
```

Maria SRE: That `OCSP response: no response sent` is a red flag — their egress likely blocks OCSP responders (or proxies are stripping stapled OCSP). Common culprits: outbound allowlist missing ocsp.int-x3.letsencrypt.org (and other CA OCSP hosts), SNI-mangling proxies, or TLS MITM appliances. Ask them to test from a host with no proxy: `curl --resolve pypi.org:443:151.101.0.223 -v https://pypi.org/simple/` to see if SNI/hostname mapping is the issue.

Alex W: Proposed minimal allowlist we normally provide for Private installs (names + ports):
- DNS: TCP/UDP 53 (their resolver to internet)
- NTP: UDP 123
- Package registries: `pypi.org`, `files.pythonhosted.org`, `pypi.io` (443)
- Debian/Ubuntu apt: `archive.ubuntu.com`, `security.ubuntu.com`, `deb.debian.org` (80/443)
- Container registries: `ghcr.io`, `registry-1.docker.io`, `auth.docker.io` (443)
- Model & runtime endpoints: `models.redwood.ai`, `registry.redwood.ai`, `model-storage.redwood.ai` (443)
- Auth/service control: `auth.redwood.ai`, `token.redwood.ai` (443)
- Telemetry/ingest: `ingest.redwood.ai`, `telemetry.redwood.ai` (443)
- CA/OCSP/CRL endpoints: `ocsp.int-x3.letsencrypt.org`, `r3.o.lencr.org`, `ocsp.sectigo.com`, plus CRL endpoints for major CAs (443)
- Package signing & download mirrors: `files.pythonhosted.org` (443), `pypi.org` (443), `launchpad.net` (443)

Also allow TLS SNI passthrough (no active MITM) and avoid intercepting certs for our service domains. If they only whitelist IPs, warn that cloud IPs can change; recommend hostnames or managed proxy with TLS passthrough.

Leo (support): Customer asked which ports for OCSP — answer is TCP 80 and 443 depending on CA, but many OCSP responders use 443. Also remind them to allow outbound UDP/TCP 53 for DNS.

Maria SRE: Quick troubleshooting checklist to run and paste results here (one-liners):
1) `curl -vI https://files.pythonhosted.org/simple/`
2) `openssl s_client -connect files.pythonhosted.org:443 -status -servername files.pythonhosted.org`
3) `dig +short pypi.org` and `dig +short files.pythonhosted.org` (check DNS resolution)
4) `curl -v https://ocsp.int-x3.letsencrypt.org` (should respond or at least connect)
5) `docker login ghcr.io` (see if auth redirects work)

deploy-bot: :white_check_mark: Customer ran 1-3 and posted results; attaching trimmed output from their host:```
> curl -vI https://files.pythonhosted.org/simple/
* Connected to files.pythonhosted.org (151.101.0.223) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake: CLIENT HELLO
* server certificate verification OK
* TLS handshake: SERVER HELLO
* OCSP response: no response sent
* curl: (35) error:14077410:SSL routines:SSL23_GET_SERVER_HELLO:tlsv1 alert protocol version

> dig +short files.pythonhosted.org
151.101.0.223
```

Alex W: Based on that: allowlist OCSP responders + ensure their proxy isn't downgrading TLS. Next steps for us:
- Share the full host list above with customer (recommend hostname-based allowlist).
- If they can, ask them to temporarily enable direct outbound to confirm — if direct works, shows proxy issue.
- If they must use IP allowlist only, we can provide commonly observed IP blocks for github/fastly/pypi but note these can change and are fragile.

Leo (support): I'll push the host list and the checklist to the customer and ask for the `openssl s_client -status` output for `registry.redwood.ai` and `ocsp` access. Will follow up here. Thanks everyone. :pray:

Maria SRE: If they still see `403` from GHCR for container pulls, check whether their egress IPs are being geo-blocked by GitHub's CDN — sometimes requiring support tickets with GitHub. Also verify MTU/path issues if TCP resets show up.

Alex W: FYI — for Private installs we document these endpoints in the README under "Firewall/Egress Requirements"; will open a quick PR to include explicit OCSP hosts and a short note about SNI/TLS passthrough.

Leo (support): Customer acknowledged and will run checks. Thread will update when they paste outputs. :speech_balloon:
